text:
Annie: tagging the cut: inference-engine:v2.4.1-rc3 created and pinned for tonight's promo window (2026-03-21 22:00 UTC). Need signoffs and any known risks.
Ben: ack. I'll run the canary plan and own traffic steering.
Alice: note — this RC includes a KV cache layout change. First requests may hit cold KV. Recommend warming before wide promo.
Carla: kicking off quick staging smoke against rc3 now, will report back in ~5m.
deploy-bot: CI job queued: smoke-tests inference-engine:v2.4.1-rc3 (staging) — https://ci.redwood/internal/job/5567
Ben: proposed canary: 5% for 15m in NA, health gates: p95 < 280ms, errors < 0.2%. Fallback target: inference-engine:v2.4.0
Tom: add automated rollback triggers: if p95 > 300ms OR errors > 0.5% during canary, auto-shift to v2.4.0.
Annie: DB freeze 21:30-23:30 UTC this window — absolutely no migrations during promo. Call out in release notes.
Carla: smoke results: all green except one flaky rerank test (known intermittent). Logs:
```
[rerank] WARN score_norm borderline
[model] weights 1.2GB loaded
health: ok
```
Carla: overall ready from staging side. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary job created: promote --env prod --pin inference-engine:v2.4.1-rc3 --canary 5 --health p95<280ms --fallback inference-engine:v2.4.0
Ben: starting canary now.
deploy-bot: canary started (id=canary-3061234567-1) — targets: 5% NA. Live monitor: https://ops.redwood/internal/canaries/3061234567
Rachel: observing canary — a subset of requests show p95 spikes up to ~470ms on a couple hosts. GPU ok (~60%), CPU normal.
Alice: that pattern smells like KV cold-populate overhead. Which endpoints?
Rachel: /v1/generate and /v1/chat most impacted. Traces show an extra kv-populate span on first hits.
Tom: rollback commands are ready:
```
# immediate rollback
deploybot rollback --env prod --to inference-engine:v2.4.0 --reason "canary p95 spike"
# region-scoped rollback
deploybot rollback --env prod --to inference-engine:v2.4.0 --region NA
```
Tom: alt plan: drop canary to 1% and run targeted warmers against canary hosts to populate KV, then ramp.
Ben: agree. Recommend pausing further ramp until we try a warm approach. Annie — ok to pause and warm within window?
Annie: pause promo. If warm+validation finishes before DB freeze end we can continue; otherwise abort and reschedule. We can't accept a risk of client latency regressions.
Rachel: I'll run targeted warmers for top-50 prefixes hitting canary endpoints. Estimate ~6-8m to warm NA cluster.
Alice: warmer command:
```
python tools/kv_warmer.py --model inference-engine:v2.4.1-rc3 --prefix-file top50.txt --concurrency 8 --target canary
```
Carla: run warmers only against canary hosts first to avoid polluting prod metrics.
Ben: reconfigured traffic controller to hold canary and route warmers to canary hosts.
deploy-bot: canary paused (id=canary-3061234567-1) — operator_hold by Annie
Rachel: warmers running. kv populate latencies dropping from ~180ms to ~10-15ms after a few prefixes. p95 on canary now ~210ms.
Carla: re-ran smoke against canary endpoints: passes. No new errors.
Ben: recommend slowly increasing to 3% and watch for 10-15m.
Annie: okay to ramp to 3% only. No more than 3% without second signoff.
deploy-bot: scaling canary to 3% (id=canary-3061234567-1) — action OK
Ben: monitoring: after 9m at 3% p95=218ms, error=0.04% steady.
Tom: if metrics hold for 15m, I support moving to 10%. Keep rollback hook ready.
Annie: Ben, ping me after 10m for final thumbs. Great quick detection and response on the cache issue. :raised_hands:
Rachel: saving trace slices and adding a small checklist item to post-release tasks: include KV-warm step for future rc with cache schema changes — https://docs.redwood/internal/release-checklist#kv-warm
Annie: holding thread until full promo done. If anything degrades we abort promo and roll back. Otherwise proceed with staged ramp per plan.
Ben: ack. Will update status through completion.
